questions.q: A 32-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. Inguinal lymph nodes are firm, non-tender, and rubbery. Dark-field microscopy of the ulcer discharge shows motile spirochetes. What is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose is the drug of choice for primary, secondary, and early latent syphilis per WHO/CDC guidelines.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with a chronic ulcer on his right foot with blackish granules draining from sinuses. Microscopy reveals hyaline, broad, septate hyphae with chlamydoconidia. X-ray shows 'dot-in-circle' sign. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Eumycetoma is caused by true fungi (e.g., Madurella mycetomatis). Black grains, broad septate hyphae, and 'dot-in-circle' sign on MRI/X-ray are characteristic. Actinomycetoma produces filamentous bacteria with different grain morphology.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops extensive epidermal detachment covering 35% BSA after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 days ago. Nikolsky sign is positive. Mucous membranes are severely involved. What scoring system best predicts mortality in this condition?
questions.exp: SCORTEN (SCORe of Toxic Epidermal Necrosis) uses 7 parameters (age, malignancy, BSA, HR, BUN, glucose, bicarbonate) to predict mortality in Stevens-Johnson syndrome/Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis. Each parameter scores 1 point; higher score = higher mortality.

questions.q: A 55-year-old diabetic presents with a crusted, honey-colored plaque on the shin that is slowly enlarging. Biopsy shows intraepidermal subcorneal pustules with neutrophils. Gram stain reveals Gram-positive cocci in chains. What is the most appropriate topical antibiotic?
questions.exp: Impetigo caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Group A Streptococcus. Mupirocin 2% is first-line topical antibiotic with high efficacy against both pathogens. Fusidic acid is an alternative but mupirocin is preferred for limited impetigo.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with multiple hypopigmented macules on the trunk with fine branny scales. KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (also known as Pityrosporum orbiculare). KOH mount shows short hyphae and spherical yeast cells resembling 'spaghetti and meatballs' (or 'banana and grapes').

questions.q: A 40-year-old lepromatous leprosy patient on MDT for 6 months develops sudden onset fever, tender erythematous nodules over the face and extremities, and iridocyclitis. Lepra bacilli load in slit-skin smear is 4+. What is this reaction and its treatment?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL/Type 2 reaction) occurs in lepromatous (LL) and borderline lepromatous (BL) leprosy. It is an immune-complex mediated reaction. Thalidomide is the drug of choice for severe ENL; prednisolone is used when thalidomide is contraindicated.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with a butterfly-shaped erythematous rash across the malar area sparing the nasolabial folds, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive at 1:640. Which antibody is most specific for this diagnosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibody is highly specific (>95%) for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), though not very sensitive (~25%). Anti-dsDNA is also specific but Anti-Sm is considered the most specific. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with flaccid blisters on normal-appearing skin. Biopsy shows intraepidermal acantholysis with tombstone row of basal cells. Direct immunofluorescence shows fishnet/chicken-wire pattern of IgG deposits. What is the target antigen?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets Desmoglein 3 (DSG3) predominantly, leading to mucocutaneous involvement. Desmoglein 1 is targeted in pemphigus foliaceus (superficial blisters, no mucosal involvement). BP180 is the target in bullous pemphigoid.

questions.q: A 25-year-old with well-defined silvery-scaled plaques on elbows and knees shows improvement with narrowband UVB therapy. A new scoring system to assess extent shows PASI 15. Which biologic agent specifically targets IL-17A?
questions.exp: Ixekizumab specifically targets IL-17A. Secukinumab also targets IL-17A. Ustekinumab targets the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23. Adalimumab is an anti-TNF-alpha agent. For IL-17A specifically: Ixekizumab, Secukinumab, and Bimekizumab.

questions.q: A healthcare worker presents with vesicular lesions on the finger after contact with a patient's herpetic lesion. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. What is this condition called?
questions.exp: Herpetic whitlow is a painful HSV infection of the finger/hand, common in healthcare workers exposed to oral secretions (HSV-1) or genital lesions (HSV-2). Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. Treatment is oral acyclovir.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasias on the alar rim of his nose. Dermoscopy shows arborizing vessels and blue-grey ovoid nests. What is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Wide local excision with 5 mm margin
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) in the H-zone (central face, periorbital, nose, ears) is best treated with Mohs micrographic surgery due to highest cure rates (99%) and maximal tissue conservation in cosmetically and functionally critical areas.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with thick keratotic plaques covering most of the body surface, including palms and soles. The family history reveals similar condition in the father. Skin biopsy shows massive orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis. What is the most likely inheritance pattern?
questions.exp: Ichthyosis vulgaris (most common form) is autosomal dominant, caused by filaggrin gene mutations. Lamellar ichthyosis is autosomal recessive with thick plate-like scales. X-linked ichthyosis affects males. This presentation with family history (father affected) suggests autosomal dominant ichthyosis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with progressive difficulty opening her mouth, Raynaud's phenomenon, and salt-and-pepper pigmentation changes. Skin biopsy shows dermal fibrosis and vascular changes. Anti-topoisomerase I (Scl-70) antibody is positive. What is the most specific antibody for pulmonary hypertension in this disease?
questions.exp: In systemic sclerosis, anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is associated with limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc/CREST syndrome) and is a risk factor for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Anti-Scl-70 (topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc and interstitial lung disease.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 50 cells/μL) presents with multiple painless, pearly papules with central umbilication on the face. What is the most likely diagnosis and causative organism?
questions.exp: In severely immunocompromised HIV patients (CD4 <100), disseminated Cryptococcosis can present with molluscum-like umbilicated papules on the face. This is a key differentiator - molluscum-like lesions in an HIV patient with very low CD4 count should raise suspicion for cryptococcosis. India ink stain would show encapsulated yeast.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child presents with pruritic erythematous papules and vesicles starting on the scalp and face, spreading centrifugally to the trunk. Lesions are in various stages (macules, papules, vesicles, crusts simultaneously). What complication is most common in immunocompetent children?
questions.exp: In immunocompetent children, the most common complication of varicella (chickenpox) is bacterial superinfection (secondary bacterial skin infection), usually by Staphylococcus aureus or Group A Streptococcus. Varicella pneumonia and encephalitis are more common in adults and immunocompromised patients.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a firm nodule with a central keratinous plug on his cheek that developed over 6 weeks, growing rapidly, and has now started to involute. Biopsy shows a crateriform architecture with central keratin, surrounded by well-differentiated squamous epithelium. What is this lesion?
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma is a rapidly growing, self-involuting epithelial neoplasm with characteristic crateriform architecture on histology. It grows over 4-6 weeks then spontaneously regresses over months. It is now often classified as a well-differentiated SCC variant. Excision is standard treatment to confirm diagnosis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with a solitary annular plaque with active erythematous edge and central clearing on the inner thigh extending to the scrotum. Microscopy of skin scrapings in KOH shows septate hyphae. What is the drug of choice for this condition?
questions.exp: Tinea cruris (ringworm of the groin) is treated with topical or oral terbinafine. Terbinafine (allylamine) is fungicidal and has the highest cure rates with shortest treatment duration for dermatophytosis. Nystatin is ineffective against dermatophytes.

questions.q: A 25-year-old Indian male presents with bilateral hypopigmented macules over the face and forearms with anesthesia and anhidrosis. Slit-skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows epithelioid cell granulomas with few lymphocytes but no bacilli. What is the immunological status?
opts: Lepromatous pole - high bacterial load, poor immunity
Tuberculoid pole - high cell-mediated immunity, low bacterial load
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) has strong cell-mediated immunity (high CMI). It presents with few well-defined hypopigmented macules with clear-cut margins, loss of sensation, and anhidrosis. SSS is negative. Histology shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas close to nerves. Lepromin test is strongly positive.

questions.q: During FNAC of a thyroid nodule, the dermatologist notices the patient has yellowish-orange palmar skin with normal conjunctival color. This finding is most likely due to excess consumption of which substance?
questions.exp: Carotenemia (carotenoderma) results from excess dietary beta-carotene (carrots, pumpkin). It causes yellow-orange pigmentation of the skin, especially palms, soles, and nasolabial folds. Crucially, the sclera and conjunctiva are spared, distinguishing it from jaundice where sclera turns yellow.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with recurrent genital ulcers, oral aphthous ulcers, uveitis, and pathergy test positivity. HLA-B51 is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease (International Study Group criteria) requires recurrent oral ulcers plus 2 of: recurrent genital ulcers, ocular lesions, skin lesions, or positive pathergy test. HLA-B51 is strongly associated. Colchicine is first-line for mucocutaneous manifestations.

questions.q: A 70-year-old woman on long-term diuretic therapy presents with tense blisters on an urticarial base on the thighs and abdomen. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposits at the dermoepidermal junction. Indirect IF shows antibodies that react with the epidermal side of salt-split skin. What is the target antigen?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid targets BP180 (BPAG2, type XVII collagen) and BP230 (BPAG1). It is the most common autoimmune bullous disorder in the elderly. Linear IgG/C3 at BMZ with antibodies to epidermal roof on salt-split skin distinguishes BP from epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (dermal floor pattern).

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with grouped vesicular eruptions in a dermatomal distribution along the T5 dermatome with prodromal pain. He is now 3 months post-resolution but continues to have severe burning pain at the same site. What is this condition and first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN) is pain persisting >3 months after herpes zoster resolution. First-line treatments include gabapentin, pregabalin, tricyclic antidepressants (amitriptyline), and topical lidocaine. Acyclovir treats acute infection and reduces PHN risk but is not used for established PHN.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with a painless, indurated, non-tender ulcer on the prepuce. The base is clean and the margins are undermined. Regional lymph nodes are painless. Which investigation would give an immediate diagnosis?
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Hunterian chancre) is diagnosed immediately by dark-field microscopy of serous exudate from the ulcer base, showing motile T. pallidum spirochetes. VDRL/TPHA may be negative in early primary syphilis (seronegative window period). Dark-field microscopy gives an immediate positive result.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman on methotrexate for psoriasis develops nausea, fatigue, and elevated transaminases. She is on 15 mg/week. What is the most important monitoring investigation for long-term MTX hepatotoxicity?
opts: Liver biopsy at cumulative dose of 1.5 g
questions.exp: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for detecting MTX-induced hepatotoxicity. Current guidelines recommend liver biopsy at cumulative dose of 1-1.5g, or earlier in high-risk patients (prior liver disease, alcoholism, diabetes). PIIINP is used as a non-invasive surrogate in some centers but is not yet universally validated.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a large verrucous plaque on the lower leg with satellite nodules. The lesion has been slowly growing for 15 years. Biopsy shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia with suppurative granulomas and 'copper-penny' sclerotic bodies. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis (chromomycosis) is caused by dematiaceous (melanized) fungi; Fonsecaea pedrosoi is the most common. Pathognomonic finding is muriform cells (Medlar bodies/sclerotic bodies/'copper penny' cells) - thick-walled, dark-brown, septate structures. Surgical excision + itraconazole/terbinafine is treatment.

questions.q: During patch testing, a patient shows positive reaction at D2 and stronger reaction at D4 to nickel sulfate. The surrounding skin is unaffected. What type of hypersensitivity reaction is this?
questions.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) is a Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity reaction mediated by T-lymphocytes (CD4+ Th1 cells). Patch testing detects ACD. Reaction peaks at 48-96 hours (D2-D4 reading). Nickel is the most common cause of ACD globally.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with necrotizing vasculitis of small vessels with palpable purpura on the lower limbs. Urinalysis shows hematuria and proteinuria. Serology shows elevated ANCA. Which ANCA pattern is associated with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener's)?
questions.exp: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (formerly Wegener's) is associated with cANCA (cytoplasmic ANCA), which targets proteinase 3 (PR3). Microscopic polyangiitis and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss) are associated with pANCA (anti-MPO). Skin manifestations include palpable purpura and papulonecrotic lesions.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, puffy fingers, gastroesophageal reflux, and fine bibasilar crackles. ANA is positive (1:320). Which antibody would be most helpful to determine renal crisis risk?
questions.exp: Anti-RNA polymerase III antibody is the strongest predictor of scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) in systemic sclerosis. SRC presents with acute hypertension and renal failure, more common in diffuse cutaneous SSc. ACE inhibitors are the treatment of choice for SRC.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with recurrent photosensitive eruption on sun-exposed areas. She develops erythematous annular plaques on the upper chest and back that heal without scarring. ANA is positive; anti-Ro/SSA antibody is strongly positive. What is this condition?
questions.exp: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE) is characterized by photosensitive, annular/polycyclic or papulosquamous plaques on sun-exposed areas that heal without scarring. It is strongly associated with anti-Ro/SSA (>70%). About 50% meet criteria for SLE. Hydroxychloroquine is first-line treatment.

questions.q: A liquid nitrogen cryotherapy is planned for a 1.5 cm verruca vulgaris on the palm. What is the optimal freeze time for effective treatment of a wart?
questions.exp: For verruca vulgaris (common warts), cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen requires a freeze time of 30-45 seconds to achieve a 2-3 mm lateral freeze margin beyond the visible wart. Freeze-thaw-freeze cycles improve efficacy. Shorter times are insufficient for virus destruction; longer times increase scarring risk.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with grouped papulovesicles on an erythematous base on the wrist and finger webs, also affecting the penis. The eruption is severely pruritic, worse at night. Multiple family members are affected. Which treatment applied to the whole body from neck down for 8 hours is curative?
questions.exp: Scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei) presents with intense nocturnal pruritus and characteristic distribution. Permethrin 5% cream applied from neck to toes for 8-12 hours (single or repeat after 1 week) is the first-line, safest, and most effective treatment. Benzyl benzoate and lindane are alternatives; lindane is neurotoxic and avoided in children.
